graph.title: Page 2: Architecture, Engineering and Construction (info page)
notes: This page is text and photos about the real Sears/Willis Tower. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.
The parts list (69 pieces) is noted for later pages. No ids have been used yet, so the next piece is b1.

The claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization before they can be used. This session can't run the OAuth flow, so they stay unavailable until the user authorizes them in their claude.ai connector settings. They aren't needed for this task.
This page lists facts and points of interest about the real tower. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added. The next piece id is still b1.
Step 1: the two Plate 4x10 are pushed together side by side to make an 8x10 base. They are not stacked, so neither rests on anything. The tiles in step 2 hold them together.
Step 2 shows four 1x8 tiles around the edge. I took them to be the 3 plain Tile 1x8 and the printed 'Willis Tower' tile, since the parts list has exactly those four.

Assumed layout: b3 and b4 run across the two short ends and bridge both plates. b5 is the back tile on b1, and the printed b6 is the front tile on b2. The printed tile sits at the front, where the 'Sears Tower' text shows in the picture. Which plate is front or back is a guess.
The page doesn't show which tile is which, so the order of b3 to b5 is an assumption.

Step 3: two Plate 4x6 sit side by side in the 6x8 stud area inside the black tile border. Each plate is 6 studs deep, so it crosses the seam between base plates b1 and b2. Each one therefore rests on both.

Step 4: four Tile 1x6 form a pinwheel frame on the gray plates. b9 is the left end tile and b11 the right end tile. Each end tile lies on one gray plate only. b10 (back) and b12 (front) run between the end tiles and bridge the seam between b7 and b8.
The picture shows b9 and b10 already placed and the other two going on, so the order of the last two is an assumption.

Step 5 fills the 6x4 stud area inside the gray tile frame with Plate 2x2 b13, six Jumper plates b14-b19, Tile 1x4 b20 and two Tile 1x2 b21-b22. Together these cover 24 cells, which is exactly the inner area.

Exact positions inside that area are partly a guess, so the rests_on lists for the jumpers and tiles are approximate. The gray plates are b7 (left) and b8 (right), and the seam between them cuts across the inner area. Every piece rests on b7, b8 or both.
Step 6: Plate 2x2 b23 goes on b13 at front-left. The icons for Brick 1x2 b24 and Brick 2x3 b25 are small. I read them as 3004 and 3002, the only matching bricks left in the parts list.
Which pieces b24 and b25 rest on is a guess. b24 is set on jumper b14 and b25 on jumpers b15-b18. The booklet's small dark pictures don't show it clearly.
Step 7 adds one Brick 1x3 (b26), the Curved 2x2 brick (b27) on plate b23, and one Brick 2x3 (b28).
Step 8 adds 7 Brick 1x3 (b29-b35) and 7 Brick 2x3 (b36-b42), which makes the tower shaft 2x3 studs wide. The ids follow the order the stack is built in, not the order of the parts in the box.

Course count: the stack is 13 courses of 2x3 footprint. Bottom to top: b25 (2x3), a pair of 1x3 (b26 + b29), 2x3 b28, then three more 1x3 pairs alternating with 2x3 bricks (b30+b31, b36, b32+b33, b37, b34+b35, b38). Four 2x3 bricks (b39-b42) finish the top. This matches the 8 Brick 1x3 and 9 Brick 2x3 used so far and the height in the picture.

b26 and b29 are meant to sit side by side on b25 as one course. b28 sits on that course and clutches b26 and b29, but b29 comes later in the list of ids. I listed only b25 and b26 for b28 so no entry points at a later id.
The exact order of the plain and paired courses is my reading of the brick pattern in the picture. The picture is small and dark, so this is an assumption.
In step 6 I recorded b24 as a Brick 1x2. If it was actually a 1x3 it could be the partner of b26 instead. I couldn't tell from the picture.

Step 9 adds a Brick 2x2 (b43) and a Brick 2x2 Corner (b44). Step 10 adds two Tile 1x1 (b45, b46), a Corner brick (b47) and a Brick 2x2 (b48). The step-9 picture shows the corner brick being lowered onto a 2x2 top, so b43 goes first, directly on the top 2x3 brick b42, and b44 goes on b43.
The tile placement is a guess. b45 caps the exposed stud of b43 and b46 caps an exposed stud of b42. The picture is too small to show this clearly.
The pieces in step 10 are placed in the order the icons are listed: tiles, corner, 2x2. b48 rests on b47, though the 2x2 may also clutch other studs. The step-back geometry is approximate.

Step 11 adds a Tile 1x1 (b49), a Corner brick (b50) and a Brick 2x2 (b51). The tile goes on the stud of b48 that the corner brick leaves open. b50 sits on b48. b51 is placed on b50 and on the stud of b48 that b50 doesn't cover.

Step 12 adds two Brick 1x1 (b52, b53), one long brick (b54) and a Tile 1x1 (b55). I read the long brick as a Brick 1x2 (3004), not a 1x3. Together with the two 1x1 bricks it exactly fills the 2x2 footprint of b51. The icon is small and dark, so this is a guess.
b55 is placed on 1x1 brick b52, since all of b51's studs are covered. That is an assumption.
The step-back geometry of the crown is approximate.

Steps 13 and 14 are identical: two Brick 1x1 and one long brick each. The long brick shows three studs, so I recorded it as a Brick 1x3 (3622). That leaves 2 Brick 1x3 and 1 Brick 1x2 for later pages.
Step 13 pieces are b56-b58 and step 14 pieces are b59-b61. Each one is stacked on the matching piece from the step before.

The booklet is small and dark here, so which studs of b52-b55 each brick sits on is approximate. b56 is on b53, and b57 and b58 share b54. b58 and b61 are 1x3 bricks that may overhang. The two prongs at the top are built up in parallel.
Step 15 adds three Tile 1x1 on top of the three prongs. They go on b59, b60 and b61, the tops of the stacks from steps 13-14.

Step 16 adds three bricks stacked into one tall column. The icon is dark and small. I used the parts that remain in the parts list: two Brick 1x3 (3622) and one Brick 1x2 (3004). I put the 1x2 on top, because the picture shows two studs at the top of the column.
The column goes on the free studs of b61. A tile can't carry bricks, so which tower stack the column sits on is an assumption. The tower top positions are approximate.
Step 17 puts the two white antennas on the two studs of the top Brick 1x2 (b67). This uses the last pieces in the parts list, so all 69 are now placed.
This page is the parts inventory and customer service contacts. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Its quantities match the supplied parts list. The only difference is the Tile 1x8 count: the page shows 4x 416226, which is the 3 plain tiles plus the printed one.
This page is a statement from the model's designer, Adam Reed Tucker, with a photo. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
This page is an introduction to the LEGO Architecture line. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
This is the back cover, showing other sets in the landmark series. It has no building step, so nothing is added. All 69 pieces were placed on pages 4-12 (b1-b69).
